sources.citation: game-design: a two-gang nonmetallic (PVC) new-work device box for wood framing, a common class listed to UL 514C and described by NEMA OS 2 (cited by number). Inside about 3-5/8 in wide, 3-1/8 in tall and 3 in deep, taken as 92 × 80 × 76 mm, with 3 mm drawn walls on the sides and back, so the outside is 98 × 86 × 79 mm. Unverified: no manufacturer drawing was read for this entry; electrical-realism-reviewer to check it against public dimension drawings of the class and relabel it real-world if it holds.

game-design: computed from the inside dimensions above as a plain rectangular volume, 92 × 80 × 76 = 559360 mm³ (about 34.1 in³). It is the drawn box's volume, not a marked volume and not from any code table; a real box's marked volume is smaller (tapered walls, clamps). P4's box fill reads it.

game-design: two device yokes 46 mm apart (about the 1-13/16 in gang spacing of multi-gang wall plates, unverified), one wiring device each (UL 514C by number). A mounted device's origin sits at the inside back corner of its gang, facing out of the box (+z).

game-design: four built-in cable clamps (knock-in tabs), two in the top wall and two in the bottom, one cable each, the box clamps the cable itself; positions are on the outside wall faces, one per gang, and are not taken from a product drawing.
game-design: a new-work box nailed to the side of a stud through its flange (common practice); it takes its full width along the stud.
